title: Partner fertility-treatment screening uses a six-month first-sample window
summary: Current assisted-reproduction rules allow a six-month first-sample window, reversing an earlier three-month transposition. The comparison concerns partner gametes outside direct use.
euChange: First partner sample: within three months before donation.
nationalGap: Annex II-5.1 allows HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C screening within six months before the first gamete collection. A 2014 order had expressly changed six months to three.
nationalLaw: Order of 11 April 2008, annex II-5.1 as replaced by the Order of 5 October 2023.
consequence: The first-sample window is wider for relevant partner treatment. No actual outdated test, infection or patient harm has been established.
resolution: The current official consolidation was checked on 26 October 2026. No later correction or exact published discrepancy analysis was located in bounded searches.
caveat: Direct-use partner donations are outside this EU timing requirement. Third-party donation has separate rules. Current Code Articles R1211-25 and R1211-26, clinical risk assessment and additional testing remain relevant; no equivalent binding three-month partner rule was identified. This does not assess individual treatment safety.
review: Independent adverse review passed: current Code donor rules do not establish a three-month partner-treatment cure; root independently read the current binding annex.

comparison.before: First partner sample: three months before donation.
comparison.after: Current national first-sample window: six months.
comparison.note: The 2014 transposition expressly shortened the window; the current replacement annex widens it again.

recognitionNote: Bounded French and English searches on 26 October 2026 combined the directive, 2014 and 2023 orders, partner screening and three-/six-month terms. The earlier transposition and current rule are public; no analysis identifying this exact current mismatch was located. This does not establish first discovery.
